overview: This Senate resolution supports designating September 30, 2026, as "National Veterans Suicide Prevention Day." It cites a Department of Veterans Affairs figure of about 17.5 veteran suicides per day on average and notes that veterans make up a disproportionate share of adult suicides in the United States. The resolution stresses early intervention, connecting veterans in crisis to care, safe firearm storage and cooperation among governments, health providers and veterans groups. It also calls for remembering and supporting families who have lost a veteran to suicide and learning from their experiences. It encourages Americans and organizations to hold events raising awareness of prevention and available resources. The Senate approved it by unanimous consent on September 30, 2026.
for: Supporters say a national day of attention can help connect struggling veterans with help and make sure grieving families are not forgotten.
against: Critics say the resolution is symbolic: it does not change any law or provide new funding for veterans' mental health care.
